# liveness-hyst

## Maturity

**Grade:** 3 · S3 E2 A2 H– P3 · limited by scope (core), performance (not measured) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** core — RFC 5880 BFD / babeld link-cost estimation, as an estimator (surveyed 2026-09-30; re-assessed 2026-10-06 against that survey, no new survey: mvp -> core after latency-aware `pathCost()` — ETX loss cost + RFC 9616 RTT penalty — and the hysteretic `Selector`)

**Audit:** review 2026-07-19 · mutation 2026-08-13 · src ?

**Hardening:** fuzz n/a — no fuzz obligation under check-fuzz (initial v2 fill, not reviewed) · ct n/a — liveness hysteresis (keyword review, 2026-10-07)

**Performance:** not measured

**Evidence:** model — randomized property tests: monotone cost, recovery uniformity, bounded memory (no reference model)

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** no

A **BFD-like link-liveness estimator with hysteresis**. WireGuard has no fast
liveness signal of its own, and the paths a field fabric actually runs over —
LTE, satellite, marginal copper — flap. A naive BFD timer on top of those turns
one degraded link into fabric-wide oscillation, because every flap re-runs the
topology. This estimator combines echo-probe timing with jitter/loss statistics
([`latency-stats`](../latency-stats)) and Babel-style metric smoothing as an
**input filter** to the link-state metric: bounded detection latency without
flap-driven churn.

- **Status:** the core scope (an estimator, not a BFD implementation) is
  implemented — hysteresis kernel, latency-aware path cost, hysteretic path
  selector, trace corpus, scoring and property harness; the BFD wire protocol
  and the rest are under [Backlog / deferred](#backlog--deferred).
  **Platform:** any — the estimator never reads a wall clock; every `now` is
  caller-supplied.
- **Deps:** `netsim`, `latency-stats`.
- **Model after:** BFD (RFC 5880) liveness + Babel-style metric hysteresis.

## Compared with

Surveyed 2026-09-30 per `SURVEY-PLAYBOOK.md`; stars and activity as of that date. Only READMEs/RFCs were read; FRR's source is GPL and was not opened. This module is an *estimator* (probe outcomes in, state and cost out), not a BFD session, so there is no like-for-like library in Rust, Go or Zig; the yardsticks are the protocols it is "modeled after" and general failure-detector libraries.

Our module has none of it, by design: the caller sends probes. *(bfdd feature list: inferred from the RFC)* |

Cost estimation is bound to the daemon; babeld also measures loss per direction (Hello/IHU), which an echo prober cannot. |
| [hashicorp/memberlist](https://github.com/hashicorp/memberlist) | Go | MPL-2.0 | 4.1k | push 2026-09-29 | SWIM gossip with a probe/suspect/dead failure detector, but for cluster members, not link quality; no metric output *(inferred)*. |
| [akiradeveloper/phi-detector](https://github.com/akiradeveloper/phi-detector) | Rust | MIT | 10 | push 2024-03 | Phi-accrual detector: a continuous suspicion level from heartbeat inter-arrival times; no asymmetric up/down hysteresis, no cost output *(inferred from the name and description)*. |
| Zig ecosystem | Zig | — | — | — | Nothing comparable found (`gh search repos 'bfd protocol' --language zig`: none); sibling `health` is an HTTP health endpoint, unrelated. |

**Where we are ahead:** hysteresis is *scored*, not asserted — detection latency (≤ 1500 ticks) and spurious failovers per simulated week (budget 5) are measured over a replayable trace corpus, and the ordering key `pathCost()` is separated from the damped `state()`; no wall clock, bounded memory (64-probe ring), no allocator. **Even with babeld:** the path cost combines loss (ETX) with a Babel delay-metric RTT penalty, and path choice is damped (`Selector`: margin + hold), as babeld damps route selection. **Where we are behind:** the BFD wire protocol and interval negotiation, echo/one-way modes (loss is round-trip only), and phi-style adaptive thresholds *(→ Backlog)*.

Re-assessed 2026-10-06 (no new web survey; babeld's defaults re-read from its man page): the 2026-09-30 gap a user would hit — a loss-only cost that cannot tell an LTE path from a satellite one — is closed, so the estimator covers its main use cases (detect failure without flapping, order paths by quality, pick one without flapping); what remains is a sibling wire-protocol module and adaptive thresholds, both Backlog-grade.

## Use

```zig
const lh = @import("liveness-hyst");

var est = lh.Estimator.init(.{
    .probe_interval = 200,          // ticks; 1 tick = 1 ms by this module's convention
    .down_threshold = 1500,         // fast to distrust
    .up_threshold = 5000,           // slow to trust recovery — the asymmetry IS the hysteresis
    .metric_smoothing = 0.25,
    .degraded_loss_threshold = 0.30,
});

est.onProbeReply(now, rtt);   // a reply
est.onProbeTimeout(now);      // an unanswered probe

switch (est.state()) { .up, .suspect, .down => {} }
const cost = est.pathCost();  // ← order forwarding paths by THIS
```

### Path cost: loss + latency

`pathCost()` is in units of one nominal link cost (0 = clean and fast):

```
cost = (ETX − 1)  +  rtt_weight · rtt_penalty(srtt)  +  jitter_weight · jitter_penalty(jitter)
        m/(1−m)       srtt ≤ rtt_min → 0, linear, srtt ≥ rtt_max → 1
```

- `m` is the smoothed probe loss (`metric()`); ETX − 1 is Babel's ETX link
  cost (RFC 8966 App. A) shifted so a clean link reads 0, and grows without
  bound as loss → 1 (saturated at `max_loss`).
- `srtt` is an EWMA of the RTT with the same `metric_smoothing` weight. A reply
  feeds `min(rtt, rtt_max)` and a timeout feeds `rtt_max`, which keeps the cost
  monotone (a reply degraded to a timeout can never make a path look faster).
- The RTT penalty is the Babel delay-based metric (RFC 9616) with babeld's
  documented tunnel defaults: `rtt_min = 10`, `rtt_max = 120` (ticks = ms) and
  `rtt_weight = 1.0` (max-rtt-penalty 96 over rxcost 96).
- Jitter (RFC 3550, from `latency-stats`) is **off by default**
  (`jitter_weight = 0`): Babel does not use it, and it is not monotone in path
  quality, so enabling it voids the forwarding-safety guarantee below.

What the defaults give: with equal loss, the lower-RTT path is always cheaper
(LTE at 50 ms costs 0.36, a GEO satellite at 600 ms costs 1.0); and loss
dominates once it is large — any path with smoothed loss above
`rtt_weight / (1 + rtt_weight)` (50%) costs more than every loss-free path,
however slow. All of it is configurable:

```zig
var est = lh.Estimator.init(.{ .path_cost = .{
    .rtt_min = 20, .rtt_max = 700,   // spread the penalty over satellite RTTs
    .rtt_weight = 2.0,               // RTT may add up to two nominal link costs
    .jitter_weight = 0.5,            // opt-in; see above
} });
// .rtt_weight = 0 keeps the loss-only ORDER; .cost_fn = lh.lossOnlyCost the old VALUES;
// any `fn (lh.CostInputs, lh.PathCostConfig) f64` replaces the combination.
```

### Picking a path without flapping

The cost carries no hold of its own (a held, stale value would break the
monotone ordering). The anti-flap hysteresis is in `Selector`, where Babel puts
it too (route selection): leave a `.down` path at once, but move to a cheaper
path only after it has been cheaper by `margin` (0.2) continuously for `hold`
(5000 ticks).

```zig
var sel = lh.Selector.init(.{});            // .{ .margin = 0.2, .hold = 5000 }
const paths = [_]*const lh.Estimator{ &lte, &sat };
const idx = sel.update(now, &paths);        // ?usize; same order on every call
```

## ⚠ `state()` does not order paths — `pathCost()` does

`LinkState.rank()` gives the informal up-ness order for display and tests, but
it is **not** monotone in stream quality inside `{.suspect, .down}`: a
degraded-but-usable link is deliberately harder to fail away from than a clean
one, which is the whole point of the damping. Ordering paths by `state()` would
therefore reintroduce exactly the oscillation this module exists to remove.
`pathCost()` is the monotone key (with the default cost function, or any
cost function non-decreasing in loss and RTT, and `jitter_weight = 0`); treat
`state()` as the damped transition-*timing* signal. The contract is adjudicated
in `core.decide`.

## Verify

```
scripts/modtest liveness-hyst                         # Debug       — 26 pass
scripts/modtest liveness-hyst -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe  # ReleaseSafe — 26 pass
```

The estimator is **scored, not merely asserted**: a replayable trace corpus in
`trace.zig` runs clean, degraded, hard-failure and duty-cycle scenarios through
[`netsim`](../netsim), and `scoring.zig` measures the two quantities that trade
off against each other — detection latency after a genuine sustained failure
(target ≤ 1500 ticks) and spurious failovers over a simulated week (budget 5).
A tuning that wins on one and loses on the other fails the suite. `property.zig`
additionally pins bounded memory: the recent-probe ring is fixed-capacity, so
the footprint does not grow with the length of the probe stream.
`cost.zig` checks the path cost and the selector: equal-loss paths order by
RTT, large loss beats any RTT, jitter counts only when weighted, the cost stays
pointwise monotone across `rtt_min`/`rtt_max` for several RTT weights, and the
`Selector` does not move under ±20 ms RTT noise (whose raw costs cross over a
thousand times) or one lost probe, switches exactly `hold` after a durable
improvement, and leaves a `.down` path at once.

Provenance: clean-room from RFC 5880 (BFD), the published Babel metric
hysteresis description, RFC 8966 (ETX) / RFC 9616 (RTT penalty) and the
babeld(8) man page (for the default `rtt-min`/`rtt-max`/`max-rtt-penalty`/
`rxcost` values) — public specs and documentation, no third-party source
ported or studied, so no `NOTICE` entry is required (root
[`NOTICE`](../../NOTICE) §0).

## Backlog / deferred

- ~~(survey 2026-09-30) RTT/jitter in `pathCost()`~~ — done 2026-10-06: ETX loss cost + RFC 9616 RTT penalty, opt-in jitter, `Selector` hysteresis.
- (2026-10-06) A separate RTT smoothing weight (babeld's `rtt-decay`, default 42/256 ≈ 0.16): the RTT average shares `metric_smoothing` (0.25) today. Effort: small; fits §2.
- (survey 2026-09-30) A BFD control-packet codec and session state machine (RFC 5880 §4 packet, §6.8 state machine) as a sibling module, feeding this estimator. Users of BFD expect interoperability with FRR/bird peers. Effort: medium; fits §2.
- (survey 2026-09-30) Adaptive thresholds (phi-accrual style) instead of fixed `down_threshold`/`up_threshold`, for links whose jitter varies by orders of magnitude. Effort: medium; fits §2.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class C · oracle n/a

- **Class C** — internal algorithm or data structure — no outside exists, so correctness is defined by invariants or a brute-force reference. Not anchor debt.
- **Oracle n/a** — class C/D carries no anchor debt, so there is no oracle grade to give.

**What the tests actually contain.** local estimator "modeled after" BFD/Babel; scored via trace corpus + invariants, not wire-compat. The default RTT penalty is checked against babeld's documented formula and tunnel defaults evaluated by hand (not against babeld output); the selector's `margin` and `hold` defaults are SELF-DERIVED.
